notes: Published ex-vivo work cited by the Applicant and concurred with by FDA: 'imetelstat affected normal megakaryopoiesis solely by delaying MK precursor maturation, and such effect was reversible upon drug withdrawal ... This may account for one of the potential mechanisms of imetelstat-induced, reversible thrombocytopenia in patients.' Graded 2 (megakaryocyte effect). No concentration or magnitude is given in the review - both TBD. This maturation-delay-plus-reversibility mechanism is the nonclinical counterpart of the clinical finding that 86.3% of Grade 3/4 events resolve within 4 weeks.

source_table: Secondary Pharmacology, FDA's Assessment, Study No. GRN01 narrative (printed p47)
notes: THE MECHANISTIC ROW. Normal human bone marrow cells treated with 0, 0.9, 1.875, 3.75, 7.5 or 15 uM imetelstat; 'significantly inhibited the number of MK colony growth at >= 3.75 uM'. readout_value TBD because no colony counts or percentages are printed (Applicant Figure 1 is a bitmap). GRADED 2 PER THE IN-VITRO RUBRIC: a dose-dependent megakaryocyte effect at a CLINICALLY RELEVANT concentration. Exposure anchor computed from the review's own unit conversions: the document equates 750 ug/mL with ~150 uM (printed p48), giving ~5 ug per umol, so the popPK-predicted human Cmax of 89.2 ug/mL at the approved 7.1 mg/kg dose is ~18 uM - the 3.75 uM threshold is roughly 0.2x total human Cmax, i.e. BELOW therapeutic plasma concentration, not supra-clinical. This is the direct mechanistic explanation for the clinical thrombocytopenia and is telomerase/megakaryopoiesis-driven, not phosphorothioate platelet binding.

effect_vs_control: no inhibition of erythroid or myeloid colony number up to 15 uM
source_table: Secondary Pharmacology, FDA's Assessment, Study No. GRN01 narrative (printed p47)
notes: NEGATIVE CONTROL / LINEAGE-SELECTIVITY ROW - grade 0, is_platelet_specific FALSE (adjacent haematology kept for context). 'Imetelstat did not inhibit erythroid or myeloid colony number (although colony morphology was compromised at 15 uM), but significantly inhibited the number of MK colony growth at >= 3.75 uM.' The megakaryocyte lineage is selectively hit across the whole 0.9-15 uM range - this lineage selectivity in vitro is why thrombocytopenia (94% at the recommended dose) tracks so closely with, and slightly exceeds, the other cytopenias clinically.
